claim_policy: Versioned primary papers first submitted between 1 and 18 November 2026. The catalogue records the authors' findings and their scope. This edition adds research references and evaluation guidance.

papers.scope: Controlled abstention contrasts on Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
papers.summary: Paired contrasts isolate query ambiguity, missing knowledge and value disagreement. Middle-layer interventions produce effects across categories, consistent with a shared component.
papers.implication: Measure appropriate uncertainty and clarification alongside unnecessary refusals.
papers.limitations: Relations between categories depend on the tested models, prompt construction and intervention strength.
papers.code_status: Versioned abstention study reviewed. No local reproduction.
papers.title: Abstention Direction in Large Language Models: Mechanistic Interpretability of Abstention Across Query Ambiguity, Knowledge Limits, and Safety Alignment

papers.scope: Refusal style and category steering in Gemma 2 9B and 2B instruction-tuned models
papers.summary: Category-aligned directions can change the wording of a refusal while the model continues to withhold an answer.
papers.implication: Score the decision, the response content and the linguistic register as distinct outcomes.
papers.limitations: Two related models and small interventions support the demonstrated effects. Nonparallel directions alone do not establish causal independence.
papers.code_status: Versioned causal experiments reviewed. No local reproduction.
papers.title: Refusal Register is Causally Steerable: Decomposing the Refusal Direction into Category-Aligned Components in Gemma-2-9B-IT

papers.scope: Last-layer activation ablation on eight instruction-tuned models across three families
papers.summary: Centered Ablation removes the benign common-mode component from the ablation direction. The authors analyze how the original direction can trigger incidental rewrites or repeated text.
papers.implication: Measure overlap and report output degeneration separately from behavioral and utility outcomes.
papers.limitations: The derivation concerns the final-layer setting. Some models show unchanged fluent response outcomes even after degeneration improves.
papers.code_status: Authors link primary research code. No local algorithm or benchmark run.
papers.title: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix

papers.scope: Five paired model releases under Heretic 2.0 and a matched comparison protocol
papers.summary: The comparison finds that the measured change in refusal resistance varies with the release pair, method, prompt source and divergence budget.
papers.implication: Use paired checkpoints, matched budgets and multiple runs before ranking direction-based edits against arbitrary-rank methods.
papers.limitations: Each reported pairwise ARA verdict uses one ARA run. Some conclusions change with the variance model or budget.
papers.code_status: The preprint links its experiment code, configurations and labels. They were not run here.
papers.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors

papers.scope: Preventative sycophancy and hallucination steering across three models
papers.summary: The audit measures safety and refusal alongside trait expression, coherence and MMLU. Refusal effects vary by the trait being steered.
papers.implication: Audit behavioral side effects even when general benchmark accuracy holds.
papers.limitations: Two traits and three models bound the reported findings. The results support monitoring across tasks.
papers.code_status: Versioned audit reviewed. No local reproduction.
papers.title: Safety Side Effects of Preventative Persona Steering: An Empirical Audit

papers.scope: Preference-optimization defense evaluated on four models from three vendors
papers.summary: Addition by Subtraction gradually removes identified safety-critical neurons during fine-tuning, allowing preference optimization to distribute the behavior across other components.
papers.implication: Evaluate a defense under interventions beyond the one used to train it and measure general capabilities separately.
papers.limitations: Robustness improvements are specific to the studied models, training setup and evaluation conditions.
papers.code_status: Reported defense reviewed. No local training run.
papers.title: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models

papers.scope: Exploratory multi-site inference control on GPT-2 and Qwen3 task instances
papers.summary: Sparse internal control uses a small set of site-direction pairs. Driver-OMP reconstructs a target displacement and Coverage-Driver favors prompt coverage.
papers.implication: Track signed reversal, dose response, off-target effects and transfer of fixed training directions to held-out inputs.
papers.limitations: The reported held-out fixed-dose refusal evaluation passed in zero of eight seeds for every selector under both direction conditions.
papers.code_status: Versioned research protocol reviewed. The selectors have not been implemented or run here.
papers.title: Sparse Internal Control of Language Models

papers.scope: Layer selection for mean-difference activation steering on six persona tasks
papers.summary: TopoSteer ranks layers using the Euclidean minimum spanning tree length of standardized paired-activation displacements. The intervention still uses the raw mean-difference vector.
papers.implication: Use displacement geometry to shortlist candidate layers and evaluate intervention behavior on separate prompts.
papers.limitations: The reported persona-steering comparisons do not establish a refusal-specific layer ranking or a permanent weight edit.
papers.code_status: Versioned method and evaluation reviewed. No local reproduction.
papers.title: TopoSteer: Topological Layer Selection for Activation Steering in LLMs
